title: Used Accessories on a Returned Self-Pay PAP Therapy Equipment Unit
content:
# Used Accessories on a Returned Self-Pay PAP Therapy Equipment Unit

**Policy statement.** A self-pay PAP Therapy Equipment device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request is inspected and reconditioned for stock, not repaired for the patient, so its return inspection carries no repair cost assignment and the only amount the patient bears on it is the value of the used accessories that came with the unit.

**Scope of the return inspection.**

1. For a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request, which this policy governs, and only for such a device, a unit still within the manufacturer warranty period is inspected and reconditioned for stock instead of being repaired under the manufacturer warranty; every other patient-owned device within the manufacturer warranty period remains repaired under the manufacturer warranty at no charge, except water and drop damage, as the base repair rule states.
2. For a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request, and only for such a device, the return inspection assigns no repair cost and the patient bears only the value of the used accessories that came with the unit; every other owned self-pay device that is outside the manufacturer warranty, or has water or drop damage, remains repaired at the patient's cost as the base repair rule states.
3. For a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request, and only for such a device, the return inspection is recorded on its device record while that record is patient-owned even though the unit is no longer in the patient's hands; every other repair remains recorded only on a device the patient still has, as the base repair rule states.

## What this governs

- **Subject:** the value of the used accessories a patient bears when a self-pay unit comes back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request.
- **Result:** the used-accessory amount recorded on the unit's return inspection, in USD to the cent.
- **Where it is recorded:** on the return inspection filed by the agent on the returned unit's device record, which appears in the device's service history dated the day it is filed.

## Desk questions

**Does the patient pay for the reconditioning of the unit itself?** No. The return inspection assigns no repair cost; the only amount the patient bears on it is the value of the used accessories.

**Does a unit still under the manufacturer warranty go for a warranty repair?** Not when it is a self-pay device sent back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request: it is inspected and reconditioned for stock. A patient-owned device that is kept by the patient remains under the base repair rule.
